description:
Step 1 of fz-kdt.107's cure (cold review 2026-09-01, protoE.patch in
session scratchpad rev107/, ~8 lines, measured green). fz-kdt.104's
drop rule (stands_in_for, callsite_dispatch.rs:~183) judges domain
containment on SEMANTIC surfaces; at the {:cont,X} vs {:cont,X}|{:halt,X}
site the two arms differ only by their reducer's closure literal
(#66closure[] vs #68closure[]) at a position runtime_type_test_envelope
already erases to fun_top -- is_subtype says not-contained, so the exact
pair kdt.104 was built to kill SURVIVES, order-protected, and
probes/halt.fz returns {:done,3} under a legal arm order.

FIX: judge containment on the OBSERVABLE (runtime_type_test_envelope)
surfaces; keep the same-callee conjunct unchanged. Measured (protoE):
lib 1534/0, corpus stdout 0/579 moved, 1 canon file moves
(enum_predicate_search), arm-reversal crashers 2 -> 1, halt.fz correct
under ANY order (the narrow arm is dropped so no order can swallow
:halt).

RED-FIRST GATE: halt.fz as a drive_test fixture asserting {:halted,3}
under the arm-REVERSAL knob (red at base -- today green only by arrival
luck).

SOUNDNESS OBLIGATION BEFORE LANDING (the review's named open question,
the builder must ground it and the refuter must attack it): dropping on
envelope-containment routes a value carrying closure #68 into a body
specialized on #66 -- prove a callable position erased to fun_top is
ALWAYS invoked indirectly at the surviving body (evidence for:
probes/q3b.fz, three reducers through one shared dispatch, correct on
interp+native; evidence needed against: the CallableConstructionFact
grounding path and fz-kdt.111's grounded-closure machinery). If a
grounded-callable counterexample exists, the envelope judgement needs a
grounded-position carve-out.

comments.text:
BUILT at 788c0c21f. The fix is protoE's direction, with the prototype's
`let _ = self.semantic` cruft removed and the `semantic` field deleted
outright: `DispatchAlternative` now carries only what the runtime can see.

SOUNDNESS -- the named open question is REFUTED, and the rule does not need it.

The question was: "a callable position erased to fun_top by
runtime_type_test_envelope is always invoked indirectly at the surviving body."
FALSE, and the counterexample is live at 788c0c21f with nothing dropped:

  defmodule Pipeline do
    fn apply_twice(f, x), do: f.(f.(x))
    fn run(f, x), do: apply_twice(f, x)
  end
  fn main() do
    dbg(Pipeline.run(fn (n) -> n + 1 end, 10))
    dbg(Pipeline.run(fn (n) -> n * 3 end, 10))
  end

Means 12 then 90; prints 12 then 12 on run + interp + AOT. A function that only
FORWARDS a closure generalizes its arrow position (one shared body); a function
that INVOKES it specializes on the literal and grounds a DIRECT call to it
(specialization input type -> resolve_closure_call -> one-target
CallSiteSummary -> closure_callee_demand -> CallableDemand.targets.len()==1 ->
exact_direct_callable_layout -> TransportCarrier::Absent ->
materialize_closure_call_edge -> CallEdge::Direct). With captures it aborts
instead of lying: `fz_ref_load_int: ExpectedTag`. Filed as fz-kdt.125, gated
red by `compiler2_forwarded_closures_are_not_replaced_by_their_sibling`
(#[ignore]d). Enumerable.reduce is clean only because the recursive
reduce_cont/reduce_step cycle generalizes the reducer position to `a5`.

So the rule is grounded RELATIVELY, and that is the right ground:

  THEOREM. Let G be a runtime-indistinguishable group at a callsite. Every
  member of G asks identical questions, so the plan's rows for G are identical
  and whichever member is listed first receives EVERY value G can see -- one
  member was going to get them all, whatever arrival order the fixpoint
  produced. fz-kdt.118 removes from G every member that is not
  observable-maximal, leaving that member to receive exactly the values it
  would have received under the order that listed it first. Hence every
  (value -> body) routing reachable after the change is one some legal arm
  order already produced at base: the rule introduces no routing base could
  not produce. What it removes is base's dependence on the order.

  On the observable axes it is strictly better: the survivor's domain contains
  the dropped arm's at every position a runtime test can see, so the
  halt-swallowing mode -- a narrow arm answering for values outside its domain
  -- is gone by construction. On the erased axis it claims nothing and needs
  to claim nothing: that axis was never separable.

  Order-independence of the filter is unchanged from fz-kdt.104: question
  equality is an equivalence, same-callee is an equivalence, observable
  containment is a preorder and the drop's strictness makes it a strict
  partial order, so each class has a unique maximal survivor and no schedule
  can choose differently. Containment is transitive, so no cascade is needed.

WHY NO GROUNDED-POSITION CARVE-OUT. A carve-out ("do not drop when the callable
position grounds a direct call in the survivor") would change no answer.
Dropping a runtime-indistinguishable arm never changes a routing -- the plan
asks no question that separates the group -- so the carve-out would only
preserve a dead arm, at the price of a cross-executable RuntimeDemand read (a
new wait) inside call_destinations. Proof by the counterexample itself:
Pipeline.run's pair is MUTUAL containment, the rule's strictness already keeps
both arms, and it miscompiles anyway -- byte-identical before and after
fz-kdt.118. The cure is upstream (fz-kdt.107 step 3 / fz-kdt.125), not a
smaller or larger plan.

RED-FIRST EVIDENCE (base = 788c0c21f `stands_in_for`, gates and fixture in
place, under the reversal knob):
- a_closure_literal_does_not_shield_a_narrower_indistinguishable_twin:
  base returns Dispatch{2 arms}, head returns Direct(wide).
- compiler2_dispatch_answers_the_same_under_a_reversed_arm_order (interp):
  base ["{:done, 3}", "{:done, 1500}"] vs golden ["{:halted, 3}", ...].
- compiler2_jit_halts_a_reduce_under_either_arm_order (NATIVE, reversed=true):
  same wrong answer -- three-path, not an interpreter artifact.
- twins_that_differ_only_where_the_runtime_cannot_look_both_stay passes at
  base AND head: the boundary is deliberately unmoved.

GATES (all at head): lib 1538/0/6 (base 1534/0/5; +2 unit, +2 gates, +1
ignored known-red for fz-kdt.125), cli 24/0, matrix --test-threads=1 434/0/9
(base 431/0/9; +3 = the new fixture's run/interp/build), clippy -D warnings
clean, cargo fmt clean, cargo build --release clean. fz-kdt.104's shadow-free
permanent gate still green. canon pins 59/203/215 unmoved -- the change drops
arms, not executables.

CORPUS SWEEP base-vs-head, 580 fixtures, `fz2 run --dump backend=`:
- stdout: 0 movers. exit codes: 0 movers.
- canon: exactly ONE pre-existing fixture moves, enum_predicate_search
  (10535 -> 10515 lines, 6 hunks, 30 removed / 10 added). CLASSIFIED: two
  `List.reduce_while_cont/3` dispatch sites go 3 arms -> 2, each losing the
  `list(int)` arm whose observable domain is contained in its
  `list(int | :ok | :true)` sibling's and which was shielded semantically by
  the reducer's closure literal. Every one of the 10 added lines is a
  renumbering of the surviving graph nodes (n6 -> n4). Zero new questions,
  zero new arms, zero changed callees, zero new executables; x164/x167 are
  still in the program, still reached by their own direct callsites. This is
  exactly fz-kdt.104's sanctioned class: fewer and simpler plans.
- corpus-wide dispatch arms 76 -> 72, dispatch sites 36 -> 35 (2 arms on
  enum_predicate_search, 2 arms + 1 site on the new fixture).

CENSUS DELTA, measured through the artifact-reading gate helper
(`indistinguishable_dispatch_arms`) over fz-kdt.107's 10 fixtures + the new
one: indistinguishable arm PAIRS 27 -> 22. All of the movement is
enum_predicate_search 6 -> 2 (two 3-arm groups shrink to 2 arms each) plus the
new fixture 2 -> 1. Read against fz-kdt.107's 17-group census: 0 of the 12
closure-identity groups move (mutual containment -- that is the boundary the
new unit test pins), 2 of the 5 list-element groups shed their unreachable
`list(int)` member, and the tuple-payload group the ticket was filed for is
dissolved outright (Dispatch -> Direct).

ARM-REVERSAL SWEEP through the real binary (FZ_STRESS_REVERSE_DISPATCH_ARMS=1,
`fz2 run`, census 10 + new fixture): base 3 movers (enum_map_family exit 134,
enum_predicate_search exit 134, the new fixture wrong-answer) -> head 1
(enum_map_family, exit 134 in fz_list_head_int_ref). enum_predicate_search
stops aborting because the arm this rule drops IS the incompatible-accessor
one. The remaining aborter is fz-kdt.107 step 3's list-element class and is
named as such in the gate's doc comment, with the reproduction recipe, because
an in-process abort would take the suite down with it.

THE KNOB. `arm_order_stress` reverses each runtime-indistinguishable group --
only arms no runtime test can separate, so every order it produces is one the
fixpoint could have delivered. Per-thread (each cargo test case owns its
thread), seeded process-wide from FZ_STRESS_REVERSE_DISPATCH_ARMS so the same
perturbation drives the real binary. Production cost: one thread-local read per
multi-target callsite, and a borrow (Cow) rather than a clone when it is off.
`ReversedArmOrder` is #[cfg(test)].

DEVIATIONS (flagged):
- The red-first fixture is not halt.fz verbatim. The suspend line
  (`{:suspended, 9, #fn<7/0>}`) carries a mint-order id, which is a fragile
  golden in a tree that cares about mint order. Replacing it with a second
  reduce over a visibly different reducer keeps the identical arm pair AND
  proves the surviving body invokes the closure the VALUE carried
  (`{:done, 1500}`, not `{:done, 15}`) -- the soundness evidence in the golden
  itself.
- The permanent stress gate drives the interpreter in-process; the native half
  is the new fixture's own JIT gate plus the documented binary sweep recipe.
  An in-process JIT abort cannot be caught by libtest.
- No oracle.exs: Enumerable.reduce/3 with a raw {:cont, _} accumulator has no
  clean Elixir twin at this layer.

RESIDUE, named: runtime_type_test_envelope erases only TOP-LEVEL funcs
(types/mod.rs:1519-1525); a closure nested inside a tuple survives the
envelope and still blocks containment, even though the runtime predicate
cannot look inside a tuple either. Recursive erasure would drop more, and
would also touch jobs/dispatch.rs:306. Out of scope here; it belongs with
fz-kdt.119's per-position tuple work.

title: P1: the dispatch drop rule is blocked by closure identity at a position no runtime test can see
